items.stem: Power Apps canvas apps build logic using which formula language?

options.text: Power Fx, an Excel-like low-code formula language
options.rationale: Correct: canvas apps use Power Fx, based on Excel formulas.
T-SQL is for relational databases, not canvas-app logic.
DAX is Power BI's modelling language, not canvas-app logic.
Bicep is for Azure infrastructure, not canvas apps.

items.explanation: Correct: canvas apps use Power Fx, based on Excel formulas.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about canvas-app data are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A gallery's Items property can be set to a data source to show its records
options.rationale: Correct: binding Items to a data source displays records.

options.text: A collection is a data source local to the app and only temporary
options.rationale: Correct: collections are local, in-app, and not shared across devices.

options.text: SubmitForm writes changes directly without any data source
options.rationale: SubmitForm writes to the form's connected data source.

options.text: Connected data sources cannot be edited from the app
options.rationale: Apps can read and write to connected data sources.

items.explanation: Correct: binding Items to a data source displays records.

items.stem: Why does delegation matter when a canvas app uses a large data source?

options.text: Non-delegable operations are processed on only a subset of rows, risking wrong results
options.rationale: Correct: non-delegable queries operate on a row limit and can silently truncate.

options.text: Delegation changes the app's colour theme
options.rationale: Delegation concerns data processing, not styling.

options.text: Delegation is only about screen navigation
options.rationale: Delegation is about where data queries are processed.

items.explanation: Correct: non-delegable queries operate on a row limit and can silently truncate.
